zh.title: EASA與EUROCONTROL聯合舉辦ATCO CBTA工作坊
zh.summary: 10月27-28日舉辦CBTA工作坊，支援2029年新規實施
body: 歐洲航空安全局（EASA）與歐洲空中交通管理組織（EUROCONTROL）於2026年10月27至28日在EUROCONTROL航空學習中心聯合舉辦空中交通管制員能力本位訓練與評估（CBTA）工作坊，面向各國主管機關（NCA）。
工作坊旨在協助主管機關理解對歐盟第2015/340號管制員執照法規的修訂，該修訂自2029年1月1日起引入CBTA要求，適用於初始訓練、營運空中交通服務單位及管制員訓練機構。
與會者討論監管監督的挑戰與機遇，並聽取CANSO、GATE訓練機構、EUROCONTROL馬斯特里赫特上層區域管制中心（MUAC）、比利時監督機構及愛爾蘭航空管理局的觀點分享。
會議總結指出：實施CBTA是自歐洲共同規則建立以來最大變革，預期將帶來網路層面系統效益；早期主管機關與訓練機構交換意見至關重要；主管機關需妥善管理資源與審批時程；充分發揮CBTA彈性可釋放訓練管線效率；並需建立更結構化的跨主管機關對話以達致統一實施。
EASA與EUROCONTROL宣示將陪伴主管機關推動對新方法的理解、支持結構化對話、未來兩年在各利益相關者論壇深化討論、開發檢查員線上入門課程、推進Data4Training計畫，並考慮提供共享最佳實踐工具與專門檢查員訓練課程。雙方並同意將上述結論納入歐洲網路層面活動，以因應管制員人力挑戰並確保空中交通服務安全、高效且具韌性。

en.title: EASA and EUROCONTROL hold joint ATCO CBTA workshop for national authorities
en.summary: EASA and EUROCONTROL hosted a CBTA workshop Oct 27‑28 to prepare for 2029 ATCO licensing changes
body: The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) and EUROCONTROL jointly organised an Air Traffic Controller Competency‑based Training and Assessment (CBTA) workshop for National Competent Authorities (NCAs) on 27‑28 October 2026 at EUROCONTROL’s Aviation Learning Centre.

The workshop aimed to support NCAs in understanding the amendment to Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/340 on ATCO licensing, which introduces CBTA requirements for initial training, operational air traffic services units and ATCO training organisations from 1 January 2029.

Participants discussed the challenges and opportunities of regulatory oversight of this change and benefited from perspective‑sharing by CANSO, the GATE Training Organisation, the EUROCONTROL Maastricht Upper Area Control Centre (MUAC), the Belgian Supervisory Authority and the Irish Aviation Authority.

Key conclusions highlighted that implementing CBTA represents the most significant change to ATCO training since the common European rules were established and is likely to deliver systemic network‑level benefits; early exchanges between training organisations and NCAs are necessary; NCAs play a crucial role in managing resources and approval schedules; exploiting the flexibility of CBTA is key to efficiency gains; and a more structured dialogue across NCAs is needed for harmonised implementation.

EASA and EUROCONTROL declared readiness to accompany NCA initiatives, support structured dialogue, foster dedicated discussions over the next two years in stakeholder forums, develop a generic online introductory course for inspectors, advance the Data4Training initiative, and consider further tools for sharing best practices and a specific inspector training course. Both organisations agreed to integrate these conclusions into parallel European network‑level activities addressing the ATCO workforce challenge and ensuring safe, efficient and resilient air traffic services amid growing traffic demand.

facts.claim: EASA and EUROCONTROL jointly organised a CBTA workshop for NCAs on 27‑28 October 2026.
facts.sourceQuote: On October 27-28, 2026 EASA and EUROCONTROL jointly organised an Air Traffic Controller Competency‑based Training and Assessment (CBTA) Workshop for National Competent Authorities (NCAs)

facts.claim: The workshop supported understanding of the amendment to Regulation (EU) 2015/340 that introduces CBTA requirements from 1 January 2029.
facts.sourceQuote: to support them in understanding the amendment to the European Air Traffic Control Officer (ATCO) Licensing Regulation (EU) 2015/340 , which as from 1 January 2029 introduces CBTA requirements for initial training and operational air traffic services (ATS) units and ATCO training organisations (TOs).

facts.claim: The workshop was held at EUROCONTROL’s Aviation Learning Centre and included perspective‑sharing from CANSO, GATE Training Organisation, MUAC, Belgian Supervisory Authority and Irish Aviation Authority.
facts.sourceQuote: At the workshop held at EUROCONTROL’s Aviation Learning Centre, NCA participants discussed the challenges and opportunities of managing the regulatory oversight of this change, benefiting from valuable perspective-sharing on the impacts of the regulatory changes from CANSO, the GATE Training Organisation, the EUROCONTROL Maastricht Upper Area Control Centre (MUAC), the Belgian Supervisory Authority, and the Irish Aviation Authority.

facts.claim: Implementing CBTA is the most significant change to ATCO training since the common European rules and is expected to bring systemic network‑level benefits.
facts.sourceQuote: implementing CBTA represents the most significant change to ATCO training since the establishment of the common European rules, and is likely to provide systemic benefits at network level

facts.claim: EASA and EUROCONTROL declared readiness to accompany NCA initiatives, support structured dialogue, foster discussions for two years, develop an online inspector course, advance Data4Training and consider further tools and a specific inspector training course.
facts.sourceQuote: To support the realisation of these conclusions, EASA and EUROCONTROL declared their readiness to: accompany NCA or other stakeholder initiatives to promote further understanding of the approval and oversight of the new CBTA methodology for ATCOs

facts.claim: Both organisations agreed to integrate the conclusions into European network‑level activities to address the ATCO workforce challenge and ensure safe, efficient and resilient services.
facts.sourceQuote: As a next step, both organisations agreed to work towards integrating these conclusions into parallel, European network-level activities that will address the ATCO workforce challenge and ensure the provision of safe, efficient and resilient air traffic services across the European ATM network in the face of growing traffic demand.
